description: Use case: the Swiss vote of 28 February 2027 on lifting the ban on new nuclear power plants (amendment of the Nuclear Energy Act, indirect counter-proposal to the initiative 'Jederzeit Strom für alle (Blackout stoppen)', referendum filed with 131793 signatures). The file holds the numbers of the main studies of both sides (ETH/PSI white paper of June 2026, BAK Economics for economiesuisse of July 2026, Swiss Academies of August 2026, SES, Fraunhofer ISE, operator cost, ElCom tariffs), the pro and contra claims as supports and limits triples on the phrase 'lifting the NPP ban', and the formulas of a decision calculator: from the overnight construction cost, the cost of capital, the construction time and the capacity the levelised cost of the new plant, against the cost of the renewable alternative plus the shifted winter trade and an optional security value; the annual cost difference spread over the demand of 2050 is the average cost difference in Rp per kWh, and its ratio to a threshold gives the verdict yes, no or undecided. The BAK base case is reproduced in the calc-validation chain (12.137 TWh, 17264 million CHF, 114.4 CHF per MWh, 612 million CHF subsidy, average cost difference -0.009 Rp per kWh: undecided). The html prototype npp_ch_vote_sample.html renders this use case stand-alone. ADDITIONALLY NEEDED, marked PROPOSED NEW ELEMENT in the triple descriptions: (1) a slider field type 'calculator slider' with the field property values field min, field max and field step; (2) scenario result columns 'calculator scenario column' with a computed difference column; (3) an argument component 'calculator argument' that lists the supports and limits triples of the page phrase with the numbers of the claim phrases; (4) a verdict component 'calculator verdict' that maps a result over a threshold to yes, no or undecided with a meter; (5) in the engine a power or annuity function, because the annuity factor formula needs (1 + r)^-n and chars.php evaluates + - * / only, so the annuity factors are stored as assumed values here; (6) a max function for the subsidy need and a comparison for the verdict, or the verdict component takes the sign; (7) preset buttons that set several inputs at once (the four scenarios of the html page: ETH low, BAK base, ETH high, Academies pessimistic), which can be data as triples from the page phrase to a scenario phrase with the input values of the scenario. Values without a source are the calculator defaults and are tagged assumed with their own confidence; the measured values carry their study as source. Not in the file: the Academies report pdf itself (numbers via sda), the Axpo Energy Report 2026 and Schwarz et al. 2023 (both only via BAK), the VSE demand projection of 90 TWh, a CO2 price, risk costs and the grid expansion difference between central and decentral supply.

formulas.name: annual production formula
formulas.description: the electricity of the plant in TWh: the capacity in GW times the capacity factor times the hours of a year; GW times hours gives GWh, divided by 1000 TWh

formulas.name: interest during construction formula
formulas.expression: "interest during construction" = "overnight construction cost" * "capacity" * "WACC" * "construction time" * "interest-during-construction factor"
formulas.latex: IDC = OCC \cdot P \cdot r \cdot T_{build} \cdot f_{IDC}
formulas.description: the interest on the capital spent before operation in million CHF: CHF per kW times GW is million CHF; the factor is the share of the construction time over which the capital is on average outstanding

formulas.name: investment formula
formulas.description: the total capital until commercial operation in million CHF

formulas.name: annuity factor formula
formulas.description: the share of the investment to recover every year; NEEDS THE POWER OPERATOR, which the calculation engine does not evaluate yet (chars.php knows + - * / only), so the annuity factor is stored as an assumed value per WACC and lifetime until the engine gets a power or an annuity function

formulas.name: capital cost formula
formulas.description: the annual recovery of the investment per MWh: million CHF per TWh equals CHF per MWh

formulas.name: levelised cost formula
formulas.description: capital cost plus operating cost per MWh

formulas.name: subsidy need formula
formulas.description: what the market does not pay, in million CHF per year; zero if the levelised cost is below the market price (the engine has no max function yet, so a negative result means no subsidy)

formulas.name: alternative cost formula
formulas.description: the levelised cost of the renewable alternative plus the system cost of intermittent supply per MWh

formulas.name: shifted energy formula
formulas.description: the energy the new NPP moves from winter imports to summer exports: its production times the difference of its winter share and the winter share of the renewable alternative

formulas.name: trade value formula
formulas.description: the value of the shifted trade in million CHF per year: avoided winter imports minus lost summer exports

formulas.name: winter net import formula
formulas.expression: "winter net import with new NPP" = "winter net import" - "shifted energy"
formulas.description: the winter net import with the new NPP: the winter net import without it minus the shifted energy

formulas.name: security value formula
formulas.description: the value of the secured winter supply in million CHF per year: the shifted energy times the value per MWh the reader sets

formulas.name: cost difference formula
formulas.expression: "cost difference" = "annual production" * "levelised cost" - "annual production" * "alternative cost" - "trade value" - "annual security value"
formulas.latex: \Delta C = E \cdot LCOE - E \cdot c_{alt} - V_{trade} - V_{sec}
formulas.description: the annual cost with the new NPP minus the annual cost without it in million CHF; negative means the new NPP is cheaper

formulas.name: average cost formula
formulas.description: the cost difference spread over all consumption in Rp per kWh: million CHF per TWh is 0.1 Rp per kWh

formulas.name: household price formula
formulas.description: the household price in the scenario with the new NPP: the energy tariff without it plus the average cost difference plus grid, metering and levies; the levies value carries the grid part too

formulas.name: household bill formula
formulas.description: the annual bill of an H4 household in CHF

formulas.name: break-even construction cost formula
formulas.expression: "break-even construction cost" = ("alternative cost" + ("winter share" - "renewable winter share") * ("import price" - "export price" + "security value") - "operating cost") / ("annuity factor" * (1 + "WACC" * "construction time" * "interest-during-construction factor") / ("capacity factor" * 8760) * 1000)
formulas.latex: OCC^{*} = \frac{c_{alt} + (ws_{NPP} - ws_{ren})(p_{imp} - p_{exp} + v_{sec}) - c_{op}}{a (1 + r T_{build} f_{IDC}) \cdot 1000 / (CF \cdot 8760)}
formulas.description: the overnight construction cost at which both options cost the same: the levelised cost that makes the cost difference zero minus the operating cost, divided by the capital cost per MWh of one CHF per kW

formulas.name: verdict formula
formulas.description: a ratio below -1 is yes (new NPP cheaper by more than the threshold), above +1 is no, in between undecided; the mapping of the ratio to the three texts is the job of the proposed verdict component, because the engine has no comparison operator

Nuclear Power and the Future Swiss Energy System: A Techno-Economic Modelling Analysis. Joint White Paper by ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute, 29 June 2026. Four energy system models, 45 TWh expansion target, net zero 2050. Numbers taken from the PSI media release of the same day.

sources.name: BAK economiesuisse study 2026
sources.description: BAK Economics (2026). Volkswirtschaftliche Auswirkungen eines Ersatzneubaus der Schweizer Kernkraftwerke. Study commissioned by economiesuisse, July 2026. Base case: one EPR of 1.63 GW, commercial operation 2050, 60 years, capacity factor 85 percent, WACC 5 percent after tax, prices of 2024. Commissioned by the business federation that campaigns for a yes; the LCOE inputs come from Schwarz et al. 2023 (ETH Nexus-e) and the Axpo Energy Report 2026.
